subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Do the OpenClaw workflow-security owners approve adopting the exact `actions/create-github-app-token` v3.2.0 and `openai/codex-action` v1.11 commits in workflows that receive repository App private keys or OpenAI API-key secrets?
rationale: The patch is an automated dependency refresh, but selecting new executable third-party code for secret-bearing workflows is a repository trust-boundary choice that cannot be safely inferred from Dependabot metadata or ordinary CI success.

options.title: Audit and approve the pinned revisions
options.body: Verify the upstream commit provenance and relevant release changes for the secret-bearing actions, then approve the refreshed PR head if its workflow checks succeed.

options.title: Split out sensitive action updates
options.body: Keep routine action updates but remove the App-token and Codex Action changes for a separately owned security review.

options.title: Defer the grouped update
options.body: Close or supersede this dependency bump and wait for an owner-sponsored update if the audit cannot be completed now.

recommendation.title: Audit and approve the pinned revisions
recommendation.body: Verify the upstream commit provenance and relevant release changes for the secret-bearing actions, then approve the refreshed PR head if its workflow checks succeed.

likelyOwner.person: OpenClaw GitHub Actions workflow security owners
likelyOwner.reason: They own the repository-level decision to trust revised executable GitHub Actions in credential-bearing automation.
